subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Balance and coordination challenges
objectives: Explain what balance and coordination are

keywords.def: keeping steady while still or moving
using different parts of the body together smoothly
the area under you that holds you up
the point where your weight is centred

starter: Show a plank hold for 5 seconds.

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Clear floor and no sharp furniture nearby
Hold a wall or chair when needed
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: How balance works
bullets: Keep your weight over your base
Focus your eyes on one spot
teach.note: Demonstrate wide and narrow stance. Ask which is steadier.

teach.heading: Static balances
bullets: Tree pose with foot on calf
teach.note: Offer support. Misconception: balance means no movement; small adjustments are fine. Foot on calf or ankle, never on knee.

teach.heading: Moving balances
teach.note: Mark a line with tape if available or imagine one. Count steps.

teach.heading: Coordination challenge
bullets: Pat your head and rub your tummy
teach.note: Build to fun; it helps coordination. Encourage perseverance.

practice: What makes balance steadier: wide or narrow base?
Why do we focus our eyes on one spot?
independent: Hold a one-leg balance for 10 seconds on each leg.
exit: Combine a balance with an arm movement and hold it for 10 seconds.
lessons.send: Practise a one-leg balance each day and note your times.

lessons.title: Design a bodyweight circuit
objectives: Choose six exercises for a circuit
Perform each for 30 seconds with 15 seconds rest

keywords.def: a series of exercise stations done one after another

teach.heading: Safety first
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: What is a circuit?
bullets: Work for a short time, then rest
teach.note: Show an example list: star jumps, squats, bridges, marching, wall push-ups, tuck jumps.

teach.heading: Choose your six
bullets: One for the heart: march or jog
teach.note: Pupils choose 2 cardio, 2 strength, 1 core, 1 balance. Teacher checks safety.

teach.heading: Doing it well
bullets: Wall push-ups: hands on wall, body straight
teach.note: Model good technique. Avoid deep knee bending beyond comfort.

teach.heading: Do the circuit
teach.note: Time with a clock. Praise effort. Cool down after.

practice: Name two exercises that raise your heart rate.
independent: Practise squats and wall push-ups, 8 each, with good technique.
Decide the order of your six stations.
exit: Perform your circuit with 30 seconds of work and 15 of rest.
Write which exercise felt hardest and why.
homework: Why do we rest between stations?
lessons.send: Teach your circuit to someone at home.
